findings.claim: FIX-ROUND-1.md describes the new scp_waiver_expired entry as a '4th clause' added after 'the pre-existing three clauses', but in scp_common.rego the new clause physically appears at lines 66-69 — between clause 1 (lines 54-57, empty-string check) and the other two pre-existing clauses (lines 71-76 unparseable-string, 78-84 past-dated-string). The comment block at lines 59-65 states 'The pre-existing three clauses only handle string values' but two of those three clauses appear AFTER the new clause in the file.
findings.evidence: policies/scp_common.rego: clause-1 at lines 54-57 (expires_at==""); NEW clause at lines 66-69 (not is_string); original clause-2 at lines 71-76 (is_string + unparseable); original clause-3 at lines 78-84 (is_string + past-dated). FIX-ROUND-1.md inline-fix item 1: 'Added a 4th clause to policies/scp_common.rego scp_waiver_expired'. Dispatch-package R2 instruction: 'verify the clause is correctly placed (after the existing 3 clauses)'.
findings.impact: Purely cosmetic. In Rego v1, clause ordering is semantically irrelevant — all clauses for the same rule name are independent disjuncts. The fix is correct regardless of position. A reviewer scanning for the 'fourth' clause by counting from the top finds it second, and the surrounding comment 'pre-existing three clauses' momentarily reads backwards. No functional impact.
findings.mitigation: No functional change required. Optional follow-on: either reorder the new clause to appear after lines 78-84, or update the comment from 'The pre-existing three clauses only handle string values; without this...' to 'The other three clauses only handle string values; without this...' to avoid implying all three come before. File as TF-020Q-002 or absorb into a future cleanup pass.

self_reported_concerns: Rego absent-key interaction with new clause: verified that w.expires_at when the expires_at key is absent in Rego v1 evaluates to undefined, causing expires_at := w.expires_at to fail and the clause body to abort. Clause 1 (object.get with default '') independently handles absent key. No gap or overlap.

Full non-string type coverage for new clause: null → w.expires_at returns null, not is_string(null)=true, fires (expired); integer 12345 → not is_string(12345)=true, fires; array [] → not is_string([])=true, fires; object {} → not is_string({})=true, fires. All non-string types correctly treated as expired.

String regression: for any string expires_at, not is_string(string)=false, new clause does NOT fire. String-path clauses (unparseable at lines 71-76, past-dated at lines 78-84) are completely unaffected.
